title: Partner co-sell pipeline review - Cascade Partners
summary: Quarterly co-sell pipeline review with Cascade Partners. Reviewed three prioritized joint opportunities (Acme Retail pilot, Meridian Fintech POC, SkyeHealth expansion). Discussed technical readiness, security materials needed (SOC2/ISO docs, KMS integration), and pricing/commit asks for Dedicated offers. Agreed on follow-ups: run latency/cost benchmark for Acme, share partner pricing grid and security package, schedule an executive alignment meeting for Meridian. Action items and next steps captured.
next_steps: Redwood to share partner pricing grid and Dedicated commitment tiers (Maya) - due 2026-05-10
Liam to provision benchmark test for Acme Retail and send results (SE) - due 2026-05-14
Cascade to confirm exec sponsor for Meridian Fintech and share use case doc (Marcus) - due 2026-05-12
Schedule joint exec alignment (Maya + Marcus) - target week of 2026-05-18
action_items: Maya Chen | Send partner pricing + legal starter pack | 2026-05-10
Liam O'Neill | Run 10k-token/day latency/cost benchmark against Redwood Dedicated + Hosted for Acme | 2026-05-14

Marcus Lee | Confirm Meridian exec sponsor and provide POC success criteria | 2026-05-12
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Evelyn Park (Cascade), Marcus Lee (Cascade), Jonah Ruiz (Cascade)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, happy to kick off. Quick agenda, pipeline review, technical blockers, next steps. Evelyn you want to start with top deals?

[00:18] Evelyn Park: Yeah sure, thanks Maya. We've got three that are priority - Acme Retail, Meridian Fintech, and SkyeHealth. Acme is the most time sensitive, they're looking to roll a recommendation/assistant in pilot by end of Q3.

[00:36] Marcus Lee: For context Acme's main ask is low latency storefront recommendations and data isolation - they flagged SOC2 and VPC as must-haves, also want to see cost per 1M tokens to model economics.

[00:50] Liam O'Neill: Understood. For Acme we should probably recommend Redwood Dedicated for predictable latency and the VPC/private control plane to meet their isolation requirements. We can do a hosted pilot but there will be tradeoffs on egress and data residency.

[01:08] Jonah Ruiz: One thing to note, Acme has strict key management - they want customer-managed KMS/HSM. Does Redwood Dedicated support that in private deployments? I remember some differences between dedicated vs private.

[01:24] Maya Chen: Yes, we support customer KMS integrations for Redwood Private; for Dedicated we can integrate KMS as well but need the proper contract addendum. We'll share the KMS playbook in the security pack.

[01:40] Evelyn Park: Great. On pricing Acme is looking for unit economics, they'd prefer a reserved capacity model if it reduces per-token cost. How granular are your reserved tiers?

[01:54] Maya Chen: We have monthly and annual reserved pools with burst options. I'll send the partner pricing grid after the call. High-level, reserved commitment reduces the effective per-token/unit price and gives guaranteed throughput SLAs.

[02:10] Marcus Lee: Cool. Meridian Fintech - this one's more of a regulated POC, they'd require audit logs, RBAC, and enclave-style data handling. They've asked if Redwood can run on-prem or in a dedicated VPC in their region.

[02:28] Liam O'Neill: Technically we can do an on-prem/private deployment; there are latency and ops tradeoffs. For KV cache and batching we need to validate their sequence length distribution; sometimes long sequences break efficient batching and raise cost. We should ask for sample payloads.

[02:46] Jonah Ruiz: We can share sample payloads. Also similarly they want to compare Anthropic and VertexAI alternatives - they asked for comparative latency/cost numbers.

[03:02] Maya Chen: We can run a apples-to-apples benchmark; Liam can spin up a controlled test against Redwood Dedicated and Hosted and share results. We'll also include cost per 1k tokens and tail latency percentiles.

[03:18] Evelyn Park: Excellent. For SkyeHealth expansion, they are already on a small Hosted plan but want to scale. Security and audit retention are the key asks there as well; they may be a candidate for Dedicated if economics make sense.

[03:34] Marcus Lee: Want to dig into the sales motions - Cascade will be introducing Redwood to customers via co-sell emails and joint webinars. We want to make sure we have executive-level collateral and an easy buying path. Who owns the flow once a customer signals interest?

[03:50] Maya Chen: Typically AE owns the deal for Redwood, Cascade co-sell rep helps with introductions; for larger deals we'll do a joint exec alignment. We'll provide a co-sell one-pager and an intro email template. Priya will support onboarding and CSM handoffs.

[04:08] Priya Nair: I'll take point on onboarding readiness and will connect docs about our kickoff checklist and support SLAs.

[04:20] Jonah Ruiz: A couple of technical clarifications: what's the recommended model quantization for Dedicated GPUs for cost saving, and do you have automatic fallback to smaller models if capacity is constrained?

[04:36] Liam O'Neill: We recommend int8 quantization for many workloads; our runtime supports quantization-friendly kernels and automated fallback policies. There's also prefix/KV caching to reduce token cost but we need to validate with their prompt patterns. Also note sometimes the transcript tool hears KV cache as KV "cash" so just flagging for the notes :),

[04:58] Marcus Lee: (laughs) noted. On security compliance: can you send SOC 2 Type II, ISO27001, and your audit log retention options? Those are blockers for the Meridian team.

[05:12] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include SOC2 and ISO docs in the security pack and outline retention tiers. We'll also add the KMS and encryption at rest details.

[05:24] Evelyn Park: For the benchmarking Liam, can you include both cold-start latency and steady-state p99? Also cost per 1M tokens so we can present to procurement.

[05:36] Liam O'Neill: Yes, we'll provide p50/p90/p99, cost per million tokens for both Hosted and Dedicated and notes on how batching affects numbers. I'll run the tests with a 1k-10k token distribution to mirror Acme's range.

[05:52] Maya Chen: Good. A couple of asks from our side - Marcus, can Cascade help with securing an exec sponsor at Meridian? That helps speed procurement and legal loops.

[06:04] Marcus Lee: Yes, we'll confirm sponsor and aim to provide their name and high-level success criteria by next week.

[06:18] Evelyn Park: In terms of timeline, Acme wants an internal pilot by end of Q3 but needs procurement numbers by mid-June. If you can get pricing and benchmarking back by 5/14 that fits.

[06:34] Maya Chen: We'll target that. Any red flags on legal/contract terms from Cascade side?

[06:46] Marcus Lee: They asked about data retention and deletion policies plus liability caps. We'll send a redline request once we see the partner starter contract.

[07:00] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll send the partner legal starter pack with standard terms and a summary of negotiable items.

[07:12] Priya Nair: Also capturing onboarding SLAs for SkyeHealth if they convert from Hosted to Dedicated; we have runbooks for migration which we can share.

[07:26] Jonah Ruiz: Quick question - any limitations on model/tool calling or function calling in Dedicated deployments? We have a use case that needs structured output and tool integration for search.

[07:40] Liam O'Neill: Function/tool calling is supported; structured output is fine but we'll want to validate schema handling in the POC. In some cases streaming behaviors differ slightly between hosted and private runtimes.

[07:58] Evelyn Park: Great. Let's recap next steps and owners.

[08:06] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya to send pricing grid + partner legal pack by 5/10; Liam to run benchmarks for Acme by 5/14; Marcus to confirm Meridian exec sponsor by 5/12; Evelyn to share contact list and intro template by 5/11. We'll schedule joint exec alignment for week of 5/18. Anything else?

[08:28] Marcus Lee: One ask - can Redwood provide a short joint webinar slide deck template we can co-brand?

[08:36] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share a co-sell slide deck template along with the one-pager.

[08:44] Evelyn Park: That's all from my side. Thanks everyone.

[08:48] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in notes and send the packs.

[08:54] (call ends)

Note: transcription has minor errors (names and acronyms occasionally misheard). The call included typical sales cadence items - pricing, technical validation, security docs, and joint GTM planning.
